_meta: Region-level playbooks. A country's brief = region playbook + country highlights + country scale positions. Where a country diverges from its region, its highlights say so.

anglo.label: Anglo (US, Canada, UK, Ireland, Australia, New Zealand)
anglo.trust_currency: Task-based: track record, contracts, punctual delivery. Trust grows through demonstrated competence and reliability; two strong deliveries beat five dinners.
anglo.decision_path: Fast, individual accountability: an empowered manager decides in the meeting; decisions can be reopened when circumstances change.
anglo.communication: Low-to-mid context: say what you mean, email is direct, humor softens but does not obscure.
anglo.contract: The written contract is the deal. Deviations are negotiated as formal amendments.
etiquette: Punctuality matters (5-10 min early in North America; slightly looser in Ireland)
First names common fast in US/CA/AU/NZ; wait a beat in UK/IE formal settings
Modest gifts only, and only after a deal or at holidays (policy limits in corporates)
Small talk: sport, weather, travel — avoid politics/religion at first meeting
taboos: Overselling or exaggerated claims (instant credibility loss)
Confusing Canada with the US, or Australia with New Zealand
Assuming London slang/irony translates literally

latin-europe.label: Latin Europe (France, Belgium, Italy, Spain, Portugal, Greece)
latin-europe.trust_currency: Mixed: personal rapport opens doors, intellectual respect sustains them. Eloquence and form matter as much as content.
latin-europe.decision_path: Hierarchical with consultation: the senior cadre/patron decides; the path runs through formal channels dressed in personal relationships.
latin-europe.communication: Mid-to-high context, rhetorically rich: theory and method before conclusion (esp. France); interruption signals engagement (esp. Italy, Greece).
latin-europe.contract: Important but treated as a living framework; terms get revisited as relationships and realities evolve.
etiquette: Titles and vous/Lei formality until invited
Business lunches are real work (1.5-2h); dinner invitations are a trust milestone
Dress well — appearance signals respect for the counterpart
August vacations and regional holidays blank out decision-making
taboos: Jumping to price before establishing the intellectual frame
Public criticism or losing your composure
Treating a heated debate as hostility

germanic.label: Germanic Europe (Germany, Switzerland, Austria, Netherlands)
germanic.trust_currency: Task-based and evidence-based: credentials, precision, documented competence. Overpromising is the cardinal sin.
germanic.decision_path: Structured and deliberate: analysis first, decision once, then rigid execution. Consensus in NL/CH slows the front end and accelerates the back end.
germanic.communication: Low context, direct negative feedback: criticism of the work is normal and expected; soften it yourself, don't expect them to.
germanic.contract: Near-sacred: what is signed happens, exactly as written. Compliance and process rigor are trust signals.
etiquette: Punctuality is respect (early is on time)
Titles (Dr., Prof.) in D/A/CH until offered otherwise
Agendas are contracts; keep to them and send follow-ups in writing
Separate business meals are functional, not relationship theaters (esp. NL)
taboos: Hype, adjectives, and salesmanship
Surprise changes to a settled plan or agenda
Casual dress or chummy first-naming at first meetings (D/A/CH)

nordic.label: Nordic Europe (Sweden, Norway, Denmark, Finland)
nordic.trust_currency: Task-based with flat-hierarchy candor: honesty, modesty, consistency. Trust is high at start and lost by misbehavior.
nordic.decision_path: Consensus-first (esp. Sweden): many consultations, one durable decision; the boss facilitates rather than commands.
nordic.communication: Low-mid context, restrained: say it plainly, pause before answering, silence is comfortable. Modesty law: never claim superiority.
nordic.contract: Reliable and simple: honest terms, honest execution; disputes are rare and handled plainly.
etiquette: Flat dress code, first names immediately, minimal titles
Respect 9-to-4 meeting windows; never Friday afternoon; July and Christmas are walls
Lunch is short; the real relationship ritual is the cabin/sauna/ski invitation
Credit the group, never yourself
taboos: Self-aggrandizement or flashing wealth/status
Pressing for a decision before consensus forms
Overfamiliarity or aggressive persuasion techniques

eastern-europe.label: Eastern Europe (Poland, Czechia, Hungary, Romania, Russia)
eastern-europe.trust_currency: Personal and guarded at first: proven loyalty over time. Hospitality is generous once you're inside; skepticism is the default outside.
eastern-europe.decision_path: Top-down: the director/owner decides; formal hierarchy respected. Implementation bends around reality (improvisation is a survival skill).
eastern-europe.communication: Mid-high context with direct edges: pessimism-first framing, irony, reading what's unsaid. Russians negotiate in wide ranges strategically.
eastern-europe.contract: Treated as a power snapshot: signed, but renegotiated when leverage or circumstances shift. Detail and contingencies still expected on paper.
etiquette: Formal titles and surnames at first; flowers/odd-number customs if invited home
Vodka toasts (Russia, Poland) — pace yourself, never refuse the first
Bring documents, certificates, stamps: paperwork confers legitimacy
Strong tea/coffee hospitality — always accept
taboos: Disrespecting seniority or skipping the hierarchy
Treating signed paper as final protection without relationship maintenance
Comparing the country unfavorably to 'the West'

east-asia.label: East Asia (China, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, Hong Kong)
east-asia.trust_currency: Relationship-based: banquets, favors, time invested. Guanxi/kankei networks are the operating system — a warm introduction is worth a year of cold outreach.
east-asia.decision_path: Consensus beneath hierarchy: nemawashi/ringi (Japan) pre-aligns silently; China pre-aligns before the meeting; the senior person ratifies. Slow yes, fast execution, never reopened.
east-asia.communication: High context: what is NOT said carries the message. 'It is difficult' = no. Silence = processing. Save face for everyone, always.
east-asia.contract: The contract BEGINS the relationship (China: renegotiable as circumstances evolve; Japan: near-absolute once sealed).
etiquette: Business cards with two hands, read respectfully, laid out by seating (Japan/Korea)
Banquet seating by seniority; toast the senior counterpart first; never pour your own drink
Modest, thoughtful gifts given/received with two hands (mind anti-corruption law in China)
Punctuality absolute in Japan; keep agendas tight everywhere
taboos: Public correction or causing loss of face (mianzi/kibun) — fatal and remembered
Forcing a direct 'no' or pushing for a fast decision
White/black gift wrapping, clocks, or anything with unlucky number 4 (China)
Political small talk (cross-strait, Korea-Japan history, CCP topics)

southeast-asia.label: Southeast Asia (ASEAN: Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, Vietnam, Philippines, Laos, Cambodia, Myanmar)
southeast-asia.trust_currency: Relationship-based to the extreme: meals, family inquiries, patient time. Deals move at the speed of personal confidence, not paper.
southeast-asia.decision_path: Hierarchical with consensus performance: the senior director/patron decides privately; meetings ratify what was already socialized. Verbal signals from the senior person outweigh written process.
southeast-asia.communication: High context, harmony-preserving: 'yes' means 'I hear you'; refusals arrive as silence, deflection, or 'we will try'. Kreng jai (TH), anade (MM), hiya (PH) all suppress open disagreement.
southeast-asia.contract: A written snapshot of a relationship: useful for alignment, but reality is renegotiated verbally as circumstances change. Keep warm contact between formal milestones.
etiquette: Wai/sompeah greetings by seniority; never touch heads, never point feet (TH/KH/LA/MM)
Right hand or both hands for giving/receiving; remove shoes when entering homes/offices
Halal awareness (MY/ID): no alcohol at Malay/Muslim meals; Ramadan hours respected
Accept tea and hospitality always; decline graciously only with a reason
Monarchy (TH) and religion (monks, wats, pagodas) are sacred — zero jokes
taboos: Displaying anger or impatience — it marks YOU as untrustworthy
Public criticism or forcing a face-losing admission
Rushing to contract before the relationship is cooked
Assuming ASEAN is one culture: Singapore ≠ Indonesia ≠ Laos

south-asia.label: South Asia (India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka)
south-asia.trust_currency: Relationship-based with family-network roots: personal trust, hospitality exchanged, introducers vouched. Family firm patriarchs own decisions.
south-asia.decision_path: Steeply hierarchical: deference to seniors expected; decisions concentrated at the top, executed with jugaad flexibility below.
south-asia.communication: High context, harmony-preserving: no direct 'no'; head-wobble (India) = polite non-commitment; enthusiasm ≠ commitment.
south-asia.contract: Negotiable instrument: bargaining is a sport, timelines are elastic, renegotiation normal. Your deadlines will be enforced harder than theirs.
etiquette: Ask about family/health (avoid asking about wives directly in PK/BD)
Respect dietary codes by community (vegetarian, halal, no beef)
Titles matter (Dr./Engineer/Sir); wait for first-name permission
Tea/coffee and snacks always accepted; festival calendars (Diwali, Eid) pause business
taboos: Left hand for giving/receiving; feet/shoes pointing at people
Skip-level pressure or bypassing the senior decision-maker
Cold, purely transactional approach without a warm introducer

mena.label: Middle East & North Africa (UAE, Saudi, Egypt, Turkey, Israel*)
mena.trust_currency: Relationship-based: majlis/coffee hospitality, extended courtesy talk, family reputation. Wasta (intercession networks) is infrastructure.
mena.decision_path: Top-down via the senior male/patron: the decision-maker's private blessing is the decision; formal process follows informally settled reality.
mena.communication: High context with lavish politeness: direct refusal almost never spoken; 'insha'Allah' separates intent from dated commitment (Israel is the outlier: dugri directness).
mena.contract: Start of a relationship: terms flex as the relationship and power balance evolve; personal guarantee outranks corporate paper.
etiquette: Right hand only for giving/receiving/eating
Accept coffee/dates; shake the tiny cup to decline refill; praise the hospitality
Dress conservatively; meetings may be interrupted by phone/visitors — flow with it
Ramadan: no public eating/drinking by day, shortened hours; Friday-Saturday weekend (Gulf)
Never ask about wives/female family members
taboos: Rushing the pitch before courtesy rituals complete
Public loss of face, criticism, or showing anger
Alcohol/pork gifting; sole of shoe displayed toward anyone
Middle East politics, religion debates, or Israel/Arab conflations

subsaharan-africa.label: Sub-Saharan Africa (Nigeria, Kenya, South Africa*)
subsaharan-africa.trust_currency: Relationship-communal: extended greetings and family inquiries ARE the meeting; networks (clan, church, community) decide what org charts only record.
subsaharan-africa.decision_path: Elders and hierarchy first, then communal consultation: the senior person opens and closes; ubuntu consensus legitimizes implementation.
subsaharan-africa.communication: High context, warm, indirect on refusal: a soft answer often hides a hard no; read intermediaries and body language.
subsaharan-africa.contract: Important but relationship-negotiated: personal commitment and follow-up visits sustain terms paper alone cannot enforce.
etiquette: Greet EVERYONE in seniority order, handshake with two hands or right hand + left-hand touch for elders
Titles are mandatory (Chief, Doctor, Engineer, Pastor) — never first-name a senior
Accept hospitality generously; small thoughtful gifts honor the relationship (never bribes)
Time is event-based: meetings start when relationships are ready; build schedule slack
taboos: Skipping the greeting ritual to 'get to business'
Disrespecting elders or community structures
Left-hand exchanges; public correction of a senior person

latin-america.label: Latin America (Mexico, Brazil, Argentina, Chile, Colombia, Peru)
latin-america.trust_currency: Personalismo: the person IS the deal. Warmth, simpatía, family references, and shared meals build the confidence that paper only records.
latin-america.decision_path: Hierarchical with staged consensus: the patrão/dueño decides; meetings build the feeling of agreement that the boss ratifies.
latin-america.communication: High context, emotionally expressive: harmony-preserving ('yes' to be polite), indirect criticism, loud friendly interruption = interest.
latin-america.contract: Framework for the relationship: details flex; renegotiation is normal; personal commitment enforces more than clauses.
etiquette: Stand-up greetings, firm handshake, sustained eye contact, closer personal distance
Titles (Licenciado, Ingeniero, Don/Doña) and formal usted until invited
Long business lunches/dinners are the real negotiation arena
Accept hospitality enthusiastically; modest gratitude gifts appreciated
taboos: Cold, brusque, all-business demeanor
Public embarrassment or confrontational feedback
Assuming LatAm is one market (Chile ≠ Brazil ≠ Mexico)
US-centric comparisons or arrogance about 'efficiency'
